goals.description: Review PLAN.md and write ADRs before code

decisions: ADR-0001: Throw CurrencyMismatchException on currency mismatch; application layer owns fetch-convert-retry orchestration, keeping domain pure.
ADR-0002: LoanId wraps UUID v7 (time-sortable) with static factory method for encapsulation; callers never construct raw identifiers.
blockers: Time — did not reach code implementation (Loan, Money, tests)
reflection: Q1: today I spent almost 2 hrs completing 2 ADRs. the other 2 points are not necessarily addressed. Q2: I didn't get to it yet. Q3: it was part of the scaffolding, but it makes sense as there are accounts that can have less than 0 -> for a loan it would be like a last payment with more than you owed. Functionally it shouldn't be allowed. Rather not allowing it from a client -> therefore an exception should be thrown. - so always invalid in the end
buddy_questions_asked: What did you attempt today, and how far did you get?

The Loan constructor accepts both a principal and an outstandingBalance as separate fields, and there is a LEARNER: marker asking you to define construction invariants. Before writing anything — what relationship, if any, do you think should hold between those two values at the moment a Loan is first created, and why does the domain care?

The Money.subtract marker asks you to decide whether subtracting below zero is always invalid or sometimes part of a transition workflow. What specific Loan lifecycle event, visible in the methods on Loan.java, made you lean one way or the other on that question?
